question.prompt:
The grid below is to be filled with integers in such a way that the sum of the numbers in each row and the sum of the numbers in each column are the same. Four numbers are missing. The number \(x\) in the lower left corner is larger than the other three missing numbers. What is the smallest possible value of \(x?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_8_Q20_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The complete top row fixes every row and column sum at \(-2+9+5=12\).

Call the middle-left blank \(y\). The first column gives \(-2+y+x=12\), so \(x+y=14\). Since \(x\) must be larger than \(y\), we need \(x>7\). As \(x\) is an integer, the smallest possible candidate is \(8\).

It remains to check that \(8\) really works. The completed grid is

\[
\begin{array}{|r|r|r|}\hline
-2&9&5\\\hline
6&7&-1\\\hline
8&-4&8\\\hline
\end{array}
\]

Every row and column sums to \(12\), and \(x=8\) exceeds the other three missing numbers \(6,7,-4\). Therefore the minimum is \(\boxed{8}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\). The other printed \(8\) is not a missing number, so equality with that entry is allowed.
solutions.title: Use the fixed row sum to bound and then construct x
